new_rules.text: If the chart presents contradictory candidate encodings for browser usage and neither a visible chart legend, axis title, or annotation nor the public task identifies which of those encodings is authoritative for current market_share, then the highest-current-market_share browser cannot be uniquely determined from the supplied evidence.
new_rules.conditions: This applies when the competing readings select different browsers and the public instruction to use dashboard market_share values does not itself designate bar height or printed percentage as the authoritative encoding.

observations.location: overall chart header and plotting area
observations.content: The chart is titled "Browser Usage Share by Product"; no legend, y-axis title, or annotation identifying either bar heights or the percentage inscriptions as market_share is visible.
The green Edge bar has the inscription "87%" immediately above it, while the blue Firefox bar extends higher on the page and has the inscription "23%" immediately above it.

task_evidence.content: Use the dashboard market_share values as the evidence source; priority compatibility testing is reserved for the highest-usage browser because it has the largest user impact.

new_chains.claim: The supplied chart and task leave the authoritative market_share encoding unresolved: the percentage inscriptions favor Edge, whereas the upward bar geometry favors Firefox. The public instruction requires dashboard market_share values but does not designate one of these conflicting visual encodings, so a unique priority-browser action is not established.

refinements.condition_note: If the Edge action is ultimately selected under the printed-percentage reading, form completion also requires selecting Browser product support, Prioritize highest current usage share, and High-impact compatibility regression testing in the three required companion fields.
refinements.reason: The original chain establishes only the conditional Edge browser action; this adds the separately required workflow selections without treating them as evidence that resolves the chart-encoding conflict.

refinements.condition_note: If the Firefox action is ultimately selected under the bar-height reading, form completion also requires selecting Browser product support, Prioritize highest current usage share, and High-impact compatibility regression testing in the three required companion fields.
refinements.reason: The original chain establishes only the conditional Firefox browser action; this adds the separately required workflow selections without treating them as evidence that resolves the chart-encoding conflict.

question_responses.reason: The existing chains identify the competing readings, while the added record specifically establishes the visible and task-level support gap: neither chart nor task designates which contradictory encoding is authoritative.
Both conditional browser-action chains now explicitly include the three required companion selections needed for form completion; these selections do not resolve the unresolved market_share encoding.
